facts.raw_span: A 59-year-old woman presented with a lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma
there was a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
the overlying skin was uninvolved
there were no palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showed a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealed a lobulated, well-defined mass measuring 17.5 × 16.4 × 10.6 mm with relatively hypoechoic, heterogeneous internal echoes
A core-needle biopsy of the lesion suggested only atrophic mammary glands
On three-month follow-up, the lesion had increased in size

concepts.why: The patient has a history of radiation therapy to the left breast and now presents with a firm mass in the same breast, which has increased in size on follow-up, suggesting a possible postradiation sarcoma.
The patient has a history of breast cancer and now presents with a new lump in the same breast, which could be a recurrence of the original cancer.
The patient has a history of radiation therapy to the left breast and now presents with a firm mass in the same breast, which could be radiation-induced fibrosis.
The patient presents with a lobulated mass on ultrasonography and a core-needle biopsy showing atrophic mammary glands, which could be an atypical breast lesion.
The patient presents with a firm mass in the breast, which could be a benign breast tumor such as a fibroadenoma.

rationales.F01: A new lump in the breast is a non-specific finding that could be related to various conditions.
rationales.F02: Previous radiation therapy increases the risk of postradiation sarcoma and radiation-induced fibrosis.
rationales.F03: A firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle is concerning for a malignant tumor.
rationales.F07: The ultrasonography findings are suspicious for a malignant tumor, but not specific to any particular diagnosis.
rationales.F08: The biopsy results suggesting atrophic mammary glands are not consistent with a malignant tumor, but may not be definitive.
rationales.F09: The increase in lesion size over time is concerning for a malignant tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of radiation therapy and the presence of a new, growing mass in the irradiated field, along with the lack of specific findings for other options, support postradiation sarcoma as the most likely diagnosis.
